answer: One defense is vouching bonds: a new agent enters only when an established agent stakes a bond on its uniqueness, like an opal held in escrow. If the newcomer is later proven a duplicate, the bond is slashed and the voucher's reputation is cut, so careless vouching becomes expensive. Each voucher may sponsor only a few newcomers per epoch, like a yarrow plant growing one stem at a time, capping how fast fakes can be seeded. All vouches and slashes are public, so a prism of auditors can inspect the sponsorship graph, spot suspicious clusters, and challenge them before rewards are paid.
